references.authors: Cahill GF Jr
references.title: Fuel metabolism in starvation.
references.finding: Autobiographical review of human starvation physiology: D-beta-hydroxybutyrate, used by the brain, is what lets humans survive prolonged starvation.

references.authors: Puchalska P, Crawford PA
references.title: Multi-dimensional Roles of Ketone Bodies in Fuel Metabolism, Signaling, and Therapeutics.
references.finding: Circulating ketones are ~100-250 umol/L fed, ~1 mmol/L after a 24-h fast or prolonged exercise and up to ~20 mmol/L in DKA; the liver can make up to ~300 g/day; BHB activates HCAR2 (GPR109A) with an EC50 of ~0.77 mmol/L.

references.authors: Newman JC, Verdin E
references.title: β-hydroxybutyrate: much more than a metabolite.
references.finding: BHB reaches 1-2 mmol/L after 2 days of fasting and over 2 mmol/L on a near carbohydrate-free ketogenic diet; it inhibits class I HDACs in vitro with an IC50 of 2-5 mmol/L.

references.authors: Umpierrez GE, Davis GM, ElSayed NA, et al.
references.title: Hyperglycemic Crises in Adults With Diabetes: A Consensus Report.
references.finding: ADA/EASD consensus: DKA requires BHB >= 3.0 mmol/L plus acidosis (venous pH < 7.35 and bicarbonate < 18 mmol/L) and glucose >= 200 mg/dL or known diabetes; ~10% present euglycaemic, and very-low-carbohydrate diets are a risk factor for DKA on SGLT2 inhibitors.

references.authors: Anderson JC, Mattar SG, Greenway FL, et al.
references.title: Measuring ketone bodies for the monitoring of pathologic and therapeutic ketosis.
references.finding: Healthy people have ~0.1 mmol/L BHB and ~1 ppm breath acetone; ketoacidosis can raise BHB about 30-fold and breath acetone about 1000-fold.

references.authors: Musa-Veloso K, Likhodii SS, Cunnane SC
references.title: Breath acetone is a reliable indicator of ketosis in adults consuming ketogenic meals.
references.finding: Over 12 h of ketogenic meals, breath acetone predicted plasma BHB as well as urinary acetoacetate did (R2 = 0.54 each) and predicted plasma acetoacetate best (R2 = 0.70).

references.authors: Urbain P, Bertz H
references.title: Monitoring for compliance with a ketogenic diet: what is the best time of day to test for urinary ketosis?
references.finding: In stable ketosis (6% energy from carbohydrate), blood BHB varied over the day from 0.33 mmol/L (10:00) to 0.70 mmol/L (03:00); urine ketones were most reliably detected early morning and after dinner.

references.authors: Volek JS, Noakes T, Phinney SD
references.title: Rethinking fat as a fuel for endurance exercise.
references.finding: Defines nutritional ketosis as circulating ketones > 0.5 mmol/L reached by restricting carbohydrate for several weeks ('keto-adaptation'); argues it may benefit some athletes (hypothesis-generating review).

references.authors: Kossoff EH, Zupec-Kania BA, Auvin S, et al.
references.title: Optimal clinical management of children receiving dietary therapies for epilepsy: Updated recommendations of the International Ketogenic Diet Study Group.
references.finding: International Ketogenic Diet Study Group: classic 4:1 diet (~90% of energy from fat), modified Atkins 10-15 g/day carbohydrate rising to ~20 g, daily multivitamin, calcium and vitamin D, oral citrate to prevent stones (historic stone rate 3-7%), contraindicated in fatty-acid oxidation and pyruvate carboxylase defects and porphyria, trial for ~3 months.

references.authors: Burke LM, Whitfield J, Heikura IA, et al.
references.title: Adaptation to a low carbohydrate high fat diet is rapid but impairs endurance exercise metabolism and performance despite enhanced glycogen availability.
references.finding: Only 5-6 days of a < 50 g/day carbohydrate diet raised exercise fat oxidation to levels seen after weeks to months, raised oxygen cost by 5-8%, and acute carbohydrate restoration did not rescue race performance.

references.authors: Shimazu T, Hirschey MD, Newman J, et al.
references.title: Suppression of oxidative stress by β-hydroxybutyrate, an endogenous histone deacetylase inhibitor.
references.finding: BHB inhibited class I HDACs in cells and mice; a 24-h BHB infusion (blood ~1.2 mmol/L) raised kidney FOXO3A, MnSOD and catalase and roughly halved paraquat-induced protein carbonylation and lipid peroxidation in mice.

references.authors: Chriett S, Dąbek A, Wojtala M, et al.
references.title: Prominent action of butyrate over β-hydroxybutyrate as histone deacetylase inhibitor, transcriptional modulator and anti-inflammatory molecule.
references.finding: Across several cell types and in vivo, butyrate was a strong HDAC inhibitor but R-BHB showed no detectable HDAC inhibition and was slightly pro-inflammatory in endothelial cells.

references.authors: Youm YH, Nguyen KY, Grant RW, et al.
references.title: The ketone metabolite β-hydroxybutyrate blocks NLRP3 inflammasome-mediated inflammatory disease.
references.finding: BHB (not acetoacetate) blocked NLRP3 inflammasome activation by preventing K+ efflux and ASC oligomerisation in mouse cells and human monocytes in vitro, and BHB or a ketogenic diet reduced IL-1beta in mouse disease models.

references.authors: Neudorf H, Durrer C, Myette-Cote E, et al.
references.title: Oral Ketone Supplementation Acutely Increases Markers of NLRP3 Inflammasome Activation in Human Monocytes.
references.n: 2 crossover experiments in healthy adults (10 men in study 1)
references.finding: Raising blood BHB acutely with ketone salts or a ketone monoester increased caspase-1 activation (and IL-1beta in one study) in stimulated human blood, the opposite of the cell-culture prediction.

references.authors: Walsh JJ, Neudorf H, Little JP
references.title: 14-Day Ketone Supplementation Lowers Glucose and Improves Vascular Function in Obesity: A Randomized Crossover Trial.
references.finding: A ketone monoester (12 g BHB) before each meal for 14 days lowered 24-h glucose 7.8%, raised flow-mediated dilation from 6.2% to 8.9% and lowered stimulated monocyte caspase-1 activation, with no change in plasma cytokines.

references.authors: Taggart AK, Kero J, Gan X, et al.
references.title: (D)-beta-Hydroxybutyrate inhibits adipocyte lipolysis via the nicotinic acid receptor PUMA-G.
references.finding: D-BHB activates the niacin receptor PUMA-G/HM74a (HCAR2) at fasting concentrations and inhibits adipocyte lipolysis through it.

references.authors: Veech RL
references.title: The therapeutic implications of ketone bodies: the effects of ketone bodies in pathological conditions: ketosis, ketogenic diet, redox states, insulin resistance, and mitochondrial metabolism.
references.finding: Argues that D-BHB carries more energy than pyruvate (raising the free energy of ATP hydrolysis) so mild ketosis may help insulin-resistant, free-radical and hypoxic conditions, but notes that ketogenic diets also raise free fatty acids, which may reduce efficiency via PPAR-driven uncoupling proteins.

references.authors: Sato K, Kashiwaya Y, Keon CA, et al.
references.title: Insulin, ketone bodies, and mitochondrial energy transduction.
references.finding: In working rat hearts, adding ketones to glucose raised hydraulic efficiency by 25% (36% with insulin) by reducing the NAD couple and oxidising the coenzyme Q couple.

references.authors: Jarrett SG, Milder JB, Liang LP, et al.
references.title: The ketogenic diet increases mitochondrial glutathione levels.
references.finding: Three weeks of ketogenic diet doubled hippocampal mitochondrial glutathione and GSH/GSSG in rats by up-regulating glutamate cysteine ligase.

references.authors: Milder JB, Liang LP, Patel M
references.title: Acute oxidative stress and systemic Nrf2 activation by the ketogenic diet.
references.finding: In rats a ketogenic diet first raised hippocampal mitochondrial H2O2 and 4-HNE, then activated Nrf2 (NQO1 up) in brain and liver by 3 weeks, while liver glutathione was chronically depleted: an adaptive (hormetic) response.

references.authors: Jain SK, Kannan K, Lim G
references.title: Ketosis (acetoacetate) can generate oxygen radicals and cause increased lipid peroxidation and growth inhibition in human endothelial cells.
references.finding: Acetoacetate, but not BHB, generated superoxide (potentiated by Fe2+) and increased lipid peroxidation and growth inhibition in human endothelial cells in culture.

references.authors: Anderson EJ, Lustig ME, Boyle KE, et al.
references.title: Mitochondrial H2O2 emission and cellular redox state link excess fat intake to insulin resistance in both rodents and humans.
references.n: rodents plus a small human feeding study
references.finding: High fat intake increased the H2O2-emitting potential of skeletal-muscle mitochondria and shifted cellular redox to a more oxidised state in rodents and humans; blocking mitochondrial H2O2 preserved insulin sensitivity in rodents.

references.authors: Miller VJ, LaFountain RA, Barnhart E, et al.
references.title: A ketogenic diet combined with exercise alters mitochondrial function in human skeletal muscle while improving metabolic health.
references.finding: 12 weeks of ketogenic diet plus exercise raised muscle-mitochondrial ATP production 36% and the ATP/H2O2 ratio 36% with fat substrate vs a mixed diet, and reduced insulin resistance and visceral fat.

references.authors: Napolitano A, Longo D, Lucignani M, et al.
references.title: The Ketogenic Diet Increases In Vivo Glutathione Levels in Patients with Epilepsy.
references.finding: MR spectroscopy found higher brain glutathione in children with epilepsy on a ketogenic diet (2.5 vs 2.0 mmol/L) than in controls.

references.authors: Nazarewicz RR, Ziolkowski W, Vaccaro PS, et al.
references.title: Effect of short-term ketogenic diet on redox status of human blood.
references.finding: Two weeks of a calorie-restricted 13%-carbohydrate diet raised plasma total antioxidant status, uric acid and RBC sulfhydryls without changing RBC malondialdehyde, SOD or catalase.

references.authors: Rhyu HS, Cho SY, Roh HT
references.title: The effects of ketogenic diet on oxidative stress and antioxidative capacity markers of Taekwondo athletes.
references.finding: During 3 weeks of weight cutting, the non-ketogenic group's malondialdehyde rose while the ketogenic group's did not; ROS and SOD did not differ.

references.authors: Forsythe CE, Phinney SD, Fernandez ML, et al.
references.title: Comparison of low fat and low carbohydrate diets on circulating fatty acid composition and markers of inflammation.
references.finding: Over 12 weeks a very-low-carbohydrate diet (12% energy) lowered TNF-alpha, IL-6, IL-8, MCP-1, E-selectin, ICAM and PAI-1 more than a low-fat diet with similar calories.

references.authors: Rondanelli M, Gasparri C, Pirola M, et al.
references.title: Does the Ketogenic Diet Mediate Inflammation Markers in Obese and Overweight Adults? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.
references.finding: In overweight/obese adults ketogenic diets lowered CRP (mean -0.62 mg/dL) with a non-significant fall in IL-6 (-1.31 pg/mL).

references.authors: Feng S, Liu R, Thompson C, et al.
references.title: Effects of carbohydrate-restricted diets and macronutrient replacements on cardiovascular health and body composition in adults: a meta-analysis of randomized trials.
references.finding: Carbohydrate-restricted diets lowered triglycerides, blood pressure, CRP and TNF-alpha and raised HDL, but modestly raised LDL and total cholesterol; ketogenic versions gave larger changes.

references.authors: Drabińska-Fois N, Ogrodowczyk AM, Bauer W, et al.
references.title: Immune-modulating effects of energy-restricted ketogenic diet in women with overweight and obesity: KETO-MINOX study.
references.finding: At equal calories (1750 kcal) an 8-week Mediterranean-style ketogenic diet gave more fat loss than a standard diet; both reduced inflammatory markers and differences were gone at 1 year.

references.authors: Ang QY, Alexander M, Newman JC, et al.
references.title: Ketogenic Diets Alter the Gut Microbiome Resulting in Decreased Intestinal Th17 Cells.
references.finding: Ketogenic diets shifted the human and mouse gut microbiome differently from high-fat diets, depleting bifidobacteria (ketone bodies inhibited their growth) and lowering intestinal Th17 cells in mice.

references.authors: Hall KD, Chen KY, Guo J, et al.
references.title: Energy expenditure and body composition changes after an isocaloric ketogenic diet in overweight and obese men.
references.finding: Switching to an isocaloric ketogenic diet raised energy expenditure only ~57-151 kcal/day and did not speed body-fat loss; fat loss slowed and fat-free mass loss increased.

references.authors: Hall KD, Guo J, Courville AB, et al.
references.title: Effect of a plant-based, low-fat diet versus an animal-based, ketogenic diet on ad libitum energy intake.
references.finding: Eating ad libitum, people ate 689 kcal/day less on a plant-based low-fat diet than on an animal-based ketogenic diet over 2 weeks.

references.authors: Ebbeling CB, Feldman HA, Klein GL, et al.
references.title: Effects of a low carbohydrate diet on energy expenditure during weight loss maintenance: randomized trial.
references.finding: During weight-loss maintenance, total energy expenditure was 209 kcal/day higher on a 20%-carbohydrate diet than on a 60%-carbohydrate diet.

references.authors: Gardner CD, Trepanowski JF, Del Gobbo LC, et al.
references.title: Effect of Low-Fat vs Low-Carbohydrate Diet on 12-Month Weight Loss in Overweight Adults and the Association With Genotype Pattern or Insulin Secretion: The DIETFITS Randomized Clinical Trial.
references.finding: Over 12 months, healthy low-carbohydrate and healthy low-fat diets produced similar weight loss (-6.0 vs -5.3 kg), with no effect of genotype or insulin secretion.

references.authors: Bueno NB, de Melo IS, de Oliveira SL, et al.
references.title: Very-low-carbohydrate ketogenic diet v. low-fat diet for long-term weight loss: a meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
references.finding: At >= 12 months, very-low-carbohydrate ketogenic diets (<= 50 g/day) gave 0.91 kg more weight loss than low-fat diets, lower triglycerides, higher HDL and higher LDL (+0.12 mmol/L).

references.authors: Hallberg SJ, McKenzie AL, Williams PT, et al.
references.title: Effectiveness and Safety of a Novel Care Model for the Management of Type 2 Diabetes at 1 Year: An Open-Label, Non-Randomized, Controlled Study.
references.finding: A remotely coached nutritional-ketosis programme cut HbA1c from 7.6% to 6.3% and weight by 13.8 kg at 1 year, with hsCRP -39%, triglycerides -24%, LDL +10% and apoB unchanged (non-randomised).

references.authors: Bhanpuri NH, Hallberg SJ, Williams PT, et al.
references.title: Cardiovascular disease risk factor responses to a type 2 diabetes care model including nutritional ketosis induced by sustained carbohydrate restriction at 1 year: an open label, non-randomized, controlled study.
references.finding: At 1 year of nutritional ketosis, small LDL particles fell 21%, apoB was unchanged, LDL-C rose 10%, and hsCRP and white cell count fell; carotid IMT was unchanged.

references.authors: Lean ME, Leslie WS, Barnes AC, et al.
references.title: Primary care-led weight management for remission of type 2 diabetes (DiRECT): an open-label, cluster-randomised trial.
references.finding: DiRECT: a total diet replacement programme (825-853 kcal/day formula, not ketogenic by design) achieved diabetes remission in 46% vs 4% at 12 months, tracking weight loss.

references.authors: Goldenberg JZ, Day A, Brinkworth GD, et al.
references.title: Efficacy and safety of low and very low carbohydrate diets for type 2 diabetes remission: systematic review and meta-analysis of published and unpublished randomized trial data.
references.finding: Low-carbohydrate diets (< 130 g/day) achieved more remission at 6 months (57% vs 31%, HbA1c < 6.5%), but benefits mostly faded by 12 months, when LDL and quality of life trended worse.

references.authors: Gardner CD, Landry MJ, Perelman D, et al.
references.title: Effect of a ketogenic diet versus Mediterranean diet on glycated hemoglobin in individuals with prediabetes and type 2 diabetes mellitus: The interventional Keto-Med randomized crossover trial.
references.finding: Keto-Med: HbA1c did not differ between 12 weeks of a well-formulated ketogenic diet and a Mediterranean-plus diet; LDL rose 10% on keto vs fell 5% on Mediterranean, and keto lowered fibre and micronutrient intakes.

references.authors: Soto-Mota A, Flores-Jurado Y, Norwitz NG, et al.
references.title: Increased low-density lipoprotein cholesterol on a low-carbohydrate diet in adults with normal but not high body weight: A meta-analysis.
references.finding: On low-carbohydrate diets LDL-C rose 41 mg/dL in trials with mean BMI < 25, did not change at BMI 25-35 and fell 7 mg/dL at BMI >= 35; baseline BMI, not saturated fat, explained the variation.

references.authors: Retterstøl K, Svendsen M, Narverud I, et al.
references.title: Effect of low carbohydrate high fat diet on LDL cholesterol and gene expression in normal-weight, young adults: A randomized controlled study.
references.finding: Three weeks of < 20 g/day carbohydrate raised LDL-C 44% vs controls (individual range +5% to +107%) and raised apoB.

references.authors: Burén J, Ericsson M, Damasceno NRT, et al.
references.title: A Ketogenic Low-Carbohydrate High-Fat Diet Increases LDL Cholesterol in Healthy, Young, Normal-Weight Women: A Randomized Controlled Feeding Trial.
references.finding: A 4-week ketogenic diet (4% carbohydrate) raised LDL-C in every woman (treatment effect +1.82 mmol/L) and raised apoB and small dense LDL.

references.authors: Budoff M, Manubolu VS, Kinninger A, et al.
references.title: Carbohydrate Restriction-Induced Elevations in LDL-Cholesterol and Atherosclerosis: The KETO Trial.
references.n: 80 ketogenic dieters with LDL-C >= 190 mg/dL vs 80 matched controls
references.finding: Lean ketogenic dieters with LDL-C averaging 272 mg/dL for ~4.7 years did not have more coronary plaque than matched controls with lower LDL (cross-sectional, self-selected).

references.authors: Soto-Mota A, Norwitz NG, Manubolu VS, et al.
references.title: Longitudinal Data from the KETO-CTA Study: Plaque Predicts Plaque, ApoB Does Not: JACC Adv. 2025;4(7):101686.
references.finding: Retraction notice: the 2025 KETO-CTA longitudinal paper claiming plaque progression was unrelated to apoB was retracted at the authors' and editors' request because of methodological errors affecting data reliability.

references.authors: Kirkpatrick CF, Bolick JP, Kris-Etherton PM, et al.
references.title: Review of current evidence and clinical recommendations on the effects of low-carbohydrate and very-low-carbohydrate (including ketogenic) diets for the management of body weight and other cardiometabolic risk factors: A scientific statement from the National Lipid Association Nutrition and Lifestyle Task Force.
references.finding: National Lipid Association statement: low- and very-low-carbohydrate diets are not superior for weight loss, may help appetite, triglycerides and diabetes-medication reduction, have mixed LDL effects, and lack data beyond ~2 years.

references.authors: Shan Z, Guo Y, Hu FB, et al.
references.title: Association of Low-Carbohydrate and Low-Fat Diets With Mortality Among US Adults.
references.finding: An 'unhealthy' low-carbohydrate pattern was linked to higher mortality (HR 1.07 per 20 percentiles) and a 'healthy' plant-and-unsaturated-fat low-carbohydrate pattern to lower mortality (HR 0.91).

references.authors: Neal EG, Chaffe H, Schwartz RH, et al.
references.title: The ketogenic diet for the treatment of childhood epilepsy: a randomised controlled trial.
references.finding: After 3 months, seizures were 62% of baseline on the ketogenic diet vs 137% in controls; 38% vs 6% had > 50% seizure reduction.

references.authors: Martin-McGill KJ, Bresnahan R, Levy RG, et al.
references.title: Ketogenic diets for drug-resistant epilepsy.
references.finding: Cochrane: in children ketogenic diets increased seizure freedom (RR 3.16) and >= 50% seizure reduction (RR 5.80) vs usual care, on low to very-low certainty evidence; adult data are sparse.

references.authors: Phillips MCL, Deprez LM, Mortimer GMN, et al.
references.title: Randomized crossover trial of a modified ketogenic diet in Alzheimer's disease.
references.finding: A 12-week modified ketogenic diet (mean BHB 0.95 mmol/L) improved daily function (+3.1 ADCS-ADL) and quality of life vs a low-fat diet; cognition change was not significant.

references.authors: Gao M, Kirk M, Knight H, et al.
references.title: A Ketogenic Diet for Treatment-Resistant Depression: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
references.finding: A 6-week < 30 g/day ketogenic diet lowered PHQ-9 by 2.2 points more than a well-matched healthy control diet (P = .05), with no difference at 12 weeks or in secondary outcomes.

references.authors: Needham N, Campbell IH, Grossi H, et al.
references.title: Pilot study of a ketogenic diet in bipolar disorder.
references.finding: Pilot ketogenic diet was feasible (mean BHB 1.3 mmol/L); the one serious adverse event was euglycaemic ketoacidosis in a participant taking an SGLT2 inhibitor.

references.authors: Mela V, Ortiz Samur NS, Vijaya AK, et al.
references.title: Ketogenic diet is less effective in ameliorating depression and anxiety in obesity than Mediterranean diet: A pilot study for exploring the GUT-brain axis.
references.finding: Over 3 months a Mediterranean diet improved depression scores more than a ketogenic diet, and stool from keto participants induced anxiety-like behaviour in mice.

references.authors: Lambadiari V, Katsimbri P, Kountouri A, et al.
references.title: The Effect of a Ketogenic Diet versus Mediterranean Diet on Clinical and Biochemical Markers of Inflammation in Patients with Obesity and Psoriatic Arthritis: A Randomized Crossover Trial.
references.n: 26 adults with obesity and psoriatic disease (crossover)
references.finding: Both diets cut weight, but only the 8-week ketogenic phase significantly reduced disease activity and IL-6, IL-17 and IL-23 vs baseline.

references.authors: Burke LM, Ross ML, Garvican-Lewis LA, et al.
references.title: Low carbohydrate, high fat diet impairs exercise economy and negates the performance benefit from intensified training in elite race walkers.
references.finding: Three weeks of a < 50 g/day ketogenic diet raised fat oxidation and VO2peak but worsened exercise economy, and the 10-km race time did not improve (-1.6%) vs +6.6% and +5.3% on high or periodised carbohydrate.

references.authors: Heikura IA, Burke LM, Hawley JA, et al.
references.title: A Short-Term Ketogenic Diet Impairs Markers of Bone Health in Response to Exercise.
references.finding: 3.5 weeks of a ketogenic diet raised the bone-resorption marker CTX and lowered formation markers P1NP and osteocalcin at rest and after exercise; formation markers stayed low after carbohydrate restoration.

references.authors: Vargas-Molina S, Gómez-Urquiza JL, García-Romero J, et al.
references.title: Effects of the Ketogenic Diet on Muscle Hypertrophy in Resistance-Trained Men and Women: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
references.journal: Int J Environ Res Public Health
references.finding: Ketogenic diets without planned energy restriction did not differ from control diets for fat-free mass gain with resistance training.

references.authors: Clarke K, Tchabanenko K, Pawlosky R, et al.
references.title: Kinetics, safety and tolerability of (R)-3-hydroxybutyl (R)-3-hydroxybutyrate in healthy adult subjects.
references.finding: A single ketone monoester dose of 714 mg/kg raised blood BHB to ~3.3 mmol/L within 1-2 h (half-life 0.8-3.1 h); multi-day dosing was tolerated apart from GI effects at the highest dose.

references.authors: Stubbs BJ, Cox PJ, Evans RD, et al.
references.title: On the Metabolism of Exogenous Ketones in Humans.
references.finding: Drinks delivering ~12-24 g BHB raised D-BHB to 2.8 mmol/L with ketone ester vs 1.0 mmol/L with ketone salts (salts were 50% L-isomer); a meal cut the peak by a third; all drinks lowered glucose.

references.authors: Soto-Mota A, Vansant H, Evans RD, et al.
references.title: Safety and tolerability of sustained exogenous ketosis using ketone monoester drinks for 28 days in healthy adults.
references.finding: 25 mL (26.8 g) ketone monoester three times daily for 28 days raised BHB to ~4.1 mmol/L after each drink with no change in weight, glucose, lipids, electrolytes or kidney function; nausea after 6 of 2016 drinks.

references.authors: Cox PJ, Kirk T, Ashmore T, et al.
references.title: Nutritional Ketosis Alters Fuel Preference and Thereby Endurance Performance in Athletes.
references.finding: A ketone ester drink lowered muscle glycolysis and plasma lactate and raised intramuscular fat oxidation during exercise, even with normal glycogen and co-ingested carbohydrate.

references.authors: Valenzuela PL, Morales JS, Castillo-García A, et al.
references.title: Acute Ketone Supplementation and Exercise Performance: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
references.finding: Acute ketone supplements (esters or salts) had no effect on exercise performance (Hedges g = -0.05) from sprints to ~50-min events.

references.authors: Leckey JJ, Ross ML, Quod M, et al.
references.title: Ketone Diester Ingestion Impairs Time-Trial Performance in Professional Cyclists.
references.finding: A ketone diester before a ~31-km time trial worsened performance by ~2%, with gut discomfort and higher perceived effort.

references.authors: Poffé C, Ramaekers M, Van Thienen R, et al.
references.title: Ketone ester supplementation blunts overreaching symptoms during endurance training overload.
references.finding: Ketone ester after each session during 3 weeks of training overload blunted overreaching markers and raised sustainable training load and late-session power by 15%.

references.authors: Falkenhain K, Daraei A, Forbes SC, et al.
references.title: Effects of Exogenous Ketone Supplementation on Blood Glucose: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
references.finding: Acute exogenous ketones raised BHB by ~2 mmol/L and lowered blood glucose by ~0.5 mmol/L vs placebo, with larger effects for monoesters than salts.

references.authors: Myette-Côté É, Caldwell HG, Ainslie PN, et al.
references.title: A ketone monoester drink reduces the glycemic response to an oral glucose challenge in individuals with obesity: a randomized trial.
references.finding: A ketone monoester (0.45 mL/kg; BHB ~3.4 mmol/L) 30 min before a 75-g glucose load cut glucose AUC 11% without raising insulin.

references.authors: Bonnechère B, Stephens EB, Boileau AC, et al.
references.title: The effect of exogenous ketone bodies on cognition across health and disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: Exogenous ketones produced a small improvement in cognitive performance vs placebo (SMD 0.29) across healthy and clinical groups.

references.authors: Fortier M, Castellano CA, St-Pierre V, et al.
references.title: A ketogenic drink improves cognition in mild cognitive impairment: Results of a 6-month RCT.
references.finding: A ketogenic MCT drink (15 g twice daily) for 6 months improved several memory, language and executive tests vs placebo.

references.authors: Vandenberghe C, St-Pierre V, Pierotti T, et al.
references.title: Tricaprylin Alone Increases Plasma Ketone Response More Than Coconut Oil or Other Medium-Chain Triglycerides: An Acute Crossover Study in Healthy Adults.
references.finding: Pure C8 (tricaprylin, 2 x 20 mL) was the most ketogenic oil, raising day-long plasma ketones by ~0.3 mmol/L; coconut oil gave only ~25% of the C8 peak.

references.authors: Peters AL, Buschur EO, Buse JB, et al.
references.title: Euglycemic Diabetic Ketoacidosis: A Potential Complication of Treatment With Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibition.
references.finding: Case series describing SGLT2-inhibitor-associated euglycaemic DKA, whose near-normal glucose delayed diagnosis.

references.authors: Acharya P, Acharya C, Thongprayoon C, et al.
references.title: Incidence and Characteristics of Kidney Stones in Patients on Ketogenic Diet: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
references.finding: Pooled kidney-stone incidence on ketogenic diets was 5.9% (children 5.8%, adults 7.9%) over ~3.7 years; about half were uric acid stones.

references.authors: Churuangsuk C, Griffiths D, Lean MEJ, et al.
references.title: Impacts of carbohydrate-restricted diets on micronutrient intakes and status: A systematic review.
references.finding: Systematic review: carbohydrate-restricted diets lowered intakes of thiamine, folate, magnesium, calcium, iron and iodine by 10-70%.

references.authors: de Amorim ALB, Rodrigues EF, Sussi EL, et al.
references.title: Carbohydrate restriction during lactation: A systematic review.
references.finding: Carbohydrate restriction during breastfeeding appears repeatedly in case reports of lactation ketoacidosis requiring hospital care.

references.authors: Arsenaki E, Stathi D, Triantafyllidis KK, et al.
references.title: The effects of ketogenic diet on polycystic ovary syndrome: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: In mostly overweight women with PCOS, ketogenic diets reduced weight (-10.8 kg), LH and insulin resistance and shortened cycle length pre-post, and beat other diets for weight and LH; androgen results were inconsistent and heterogeneity high.

references.authors: Cannarella R, Rubulotta M, Leonardi A, et al.
references.title: Effects of ketogenic diets on polycystic ovary syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: High-fat ketogenic and very-low-energy ketogenic diets improved weight, glucose, HOMA, triglycerides and LH in PCOS; two RCTs found no weight advantage over low-calorie diets.

references.authors: Zhang X, Zheng Y, Guo Y, et al.
references.title: The Effect of Low Carbohydrate Diet on Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
references.finding: Low-carbohydrate diets (< 45% energy) lowered BMI, HOMA-IR and LDL in PCOS; those lasting > 4 weeks raised SHBG and FSH and lowered testosterone.

references.authors: Shang Y, Zhou H, He R, et al.
references.title: Dietary Modification for Reproductive Health in Women With Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
references.finding: Dietary interventions in PCOS increased clinical pregnancy, ovulation and menstrual regularity and lowered miscarriage; low-carbohydrate diets were the best subgroup for reproductive outcomes.

references.authors: Mavropoulos JC, Yancy WS, Hepburn J, et al.
references.title: The effects of a low-carbohydrate, ketogenic diet on the polycystic ovary syndrome: a pilot study.
references.finding: A < 20 g/day carbohydrate diet for 24 weeks cut weight 12%, free testosterone 22%, LH/FSH 36% and fasting insulin 54% in PCOS; two women conceived.

references.authors: Chavarro JE, Rich-Edwards JW, Rosner BA, et al.
references.title: A prospective study of dietary carbohydrate quantity and quality in relation to risk of ovulatory infertility.
references.finding: Highest vs lowest quintile of total carbohydrate (RR 1.91) and glycaemic load (RR 1.92) was associated with ovulatory infertility in the Nurses' Health Study II.

references.authors: Liu S, Yao Q, Li X, et al.
references.title: Effects of a ketogenic diet on reproductive and metabolic phenotypes in mice with polycystic ovary syndrome†.
references.finding: In DHEA-induced PCOS mice a 3-week ketogenic diet lowered weight and glucose, improved ovarian function in some mice and reduced ovarian inflammation and apoptosis, but impaired glucose tolerance.

references.authors: Whatley EG, Truong TT, Wilhelm D, et al.
references.title: β-hydroxybutyrate reduces blastocyst viability via trophectoderm-mediated metabolic aberrations in mice.
references.finding: Culturing mouse embryos with BHB at ketogenic-diet levels (2 mmol/L) slowed development, disturbed glycolysis and reduced fetal viability after transfer in a sex-specific way.

references.authors: Whatley EG, Harvey AJ, Gardner DK
references.title: A maternal ketogenic diet alters oviduct fluid nutrients and embryo histone acetylation in mice.
references.finding: A maternal ketogenic diet for 24-27 days raised BHB in mouse blood and oviduct fluid, delayed blastocyst development and reduced trophectoderm histone acetylation.

references.authors: Sussman D, Ellegood J, Henkelman M
references.title: A gestational ketogenic diet alters maternal metabolic status as well as offspring physiological growth and brain structure in the neonatal mouse.
references.finding: Gestational ketogenic diet lowered fertility and litter size in mice, put dams at risk of fatal ketoacidosis in lactation, and slowed offspring growth with altered brain structure.

references.authors: Zala SM, Santos R, Strasser E, et al.
references.title: Sex-dependent effects of a gestational ketogenic diet on offspring birth and lifespan.
references.finding: A ketogenic diet in the second half of mouse pregnancy reduced litter size and the proportion of female pups and shortened male offspring lifespan.

references.authors: Desrosiers TA, Siega-Riz AM, Mosley BS, et al.
references.title: Low carbohydrate diets may increase risk of neural tube defects.
references.finding: Women with restricted periconceptional carbohydrate intake (<= 5th percentile) had half the dietary folic acid and 30% higher odds of a neural-tube-defect pregnancy (aOR 1.30, 1.02-1.67).

references.authors: van der Louw EJ, Williams TJ, Henry-Barron BJ, et al.
references.title: Ketogenic diet therapy for epilepsy during pregnancy: A case series.
references.finding: Two women with epilepsy stayed on ketogenic/modified Atkins therapy in pregnancy with fewer seizures; one infant had ear deformities of unknown significance; safety not established.

references.authors: Furini C, Spaggiari G, Simoni M, et al.
references.title: Ketogenic state improves testosterone serum levels-results from a systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: Ketogenic diets raised total testosterone (by ~6.75 nmol/L with very-low-calorie KD, ~1 nmol/L with normocaloric KD), proportional to weight loss and age.

references.authors: Whittaker J, Wu K
references.title: Low-fat diets and testosterone in men: Systematic review and meta-analysis of intervention studies.
references.finding: Low-fat diets lowered total testosterone (SMD -0.38) and free testosterone (SMD -0.37) vs higher-fat diets.

references.authors: Liu CY, Chang TC, Lin SH, et al.
references.title: Is a Ketogenic Diet Superior to a High-Fat, High-Cholesterol Diet Regarding Testicular Function and Spermatogenesis?
references.finding: In obese mice, switching from a high-fat high-cholesterol diet to an MCT-based ketogenic diet for 8 weeks lowered testicular lipid peroxidation and restored semen quality.

references.authors: Myzak MC, Tong P, Dashwood WM, et al.
references.title: Sulforaphane retards the growth of human PC-3 xenografts and inhibits HDAC activity in human subjects.
references.n: mice plus a small human feeding test
references.finding: Sulforaphane inhibited HDAC in mouse tissues, and a single 68 g serving of broccoli sprouts inhibited HDAC activity in human blood mononuclear cells at 3-6 h.
